statement: Wedge mechanism: deadline-less vtime starvation under --no-rcb-time --max-timeslice disabled.
reasoning: use_rcb_time() = max_timeslice.is_some() && !no_rcb_time (detcore-model/src/config.rs:635). demo5 sets --no-rcb-time AND --max-timeslice disabled (=None), so use_rcb_time()==false: (1) RCB->vtime conversion (Detcore::update_logical_time_rcbs, lib.rs:359-475) is doubly gated off -> guest branch retirement advances vtime by ZERO; (2) no PMU preemption timer is armed (next_timeslice max_timeslice_end=None, tool_local.rs:2052) -> only preemption left is the --target-timeslice logical deadline reachable only at intercepted checkins; (3) step2d_handle_empty_queue (scheduler.rs:1989) is gated on run_queue.is_empty() AND needs a future timed_waiter; SleepUntil(LogicalTime(0)) pollers stay runnable and any target<=committed returns immediately without being inserted as a timed_waiter (scheduler.rs:2205) -> no future event to jump to; (4) per-turn add_scheduler_time creep (NANOS_PER_SCHED=500us x 500 strict multiplier) races committed_time far ahead of any guest deadline.
predicted_evidence: wedge logs: 'Skipping global time ahead'=0; SleepUntil(LogicalTime(0)) commits dominate; 0 future timed_waiter registrations in terminal spin; guest serial frozen at hpet0; committed_time creeps/races, never reaching the timer deadline.
verdict: CONFIRMED (source) as the BACKGROUND mechanism, with SCOPE CORRECTED: it is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT. A bare --no-rcb-time boot shows ALL the signatures (237 same-config A/B: Skipping=0, SleepUntil(0) dominates 558k, 0 future timed_waiters, committed races +2432s, rcbs:0) YET STILL BOOTS. The wedge additionally requires the H6 socket trigger. An earlier revision wrongly claimed the bare boot itself livelocks.

statement: Greening mechanism: rcb-time brute-forces committed_time forward across the guest timer deadline.
reasoning: With rcb-time ON, guest branch retirement advances committed_time (RCB->ns) continuously. The busy-poll/calibration loops DO retire branches, so committed_time creeps until it crosses the HPET/timer deadline in guest time, the vCPU timer fires, and boot proceeds -- slowly (fine-grained creep), hence the ~325s crawl.
predicted_evidence: booting run: committed_time advances with nonzero RCB contribution and eventually crosses the deadline; boot completes ~5x slower than pre-regression sub-minute.
verdict: CONFIRMED (source). rcb-time greens the boot because RCB->vtime keeps committed_time moving even during the poll loops, so the guest timer deadline is eventually reached. Distinct from H1's zero-advance substrate.

statement: #151 classification: --no-rcb-time EXPOSES the scheduler-vtime-jump-unproductive-pollers foundation bug; it does NOT mask a determinism bug. Re-enabling rcb-time is a legitimate STEP-BACK.
reasoning: The wedge is a deterministic guest-starvation livelock (consistent with H4 load-independence), not a masked nondeterminism. rcb-time restores a decision-deterministic (if ~5x slow) boot. So the demo config change (--no-rcb-time) is what exposed a latent foundation scheduling gap, and reverting to rcb-time is a principled step-back, not papering over a race.
predicted_evidence: the wedge is reproducible/deterministic (not seed- or interleaving-random); rcb-time boot is decision-deterministic.
verdict: CONFIRMED. Crawl boot is decision-deterministic; wedge is deterministic; --no-rcb-time exposes, does not mask.

statement: Scheduler DECISIONS are host-load INDEPENDENT (Q3, SACRED P0 gate).
reasoning: Determinism requires that no wall-clock read enters a scheduling DECISION path. If WHICH thread runs depended on host load, that is an instant P0. Test: contrast decision traces under different host loads; they must be byte-identical except verify-excluded values (committed_time wall drift).
predicted_evidence: contrasting-load decision traces byte-identical over the compared turns; only verify-excluded committed_time value drifts by ns.
verdict: CONFIRMED — Q3 P0 GATE PASSES, NO ESCALATION. Contrasting-load decision traces byte-identical over 41043 turns; only verify-excluded committed_time drifts <=238ns. The prior 'load-sensitive' verdict is confirmed-harmless (wall-clock + verify-excluded-value only). WHICH thread starves is a deterministic function of the flag/fd set, not load.

statement: Perf: the rcb-time crawl is NOT the perf fix; a foundation fix should restore sub-minute boot (Q4).
reasoning: rcb-time greens but at ~5x slowdown (crawl). Metrics: green rcb-ON ~1,000 timeslices/~200s vtime vs 3-knob busybox ~85k timeslices/~1,450s vtime vs wedge 10^5-10^6 timeslices. The crawl is a WORKAROUND; true sub-minute parity under --no-rcb-time needs a scheduler-side fix.
predicted_evidence: measured timeslice/vtime blow-up between green, crawl, and wedge; pre-regression sub-minute boot as the parity target.
verdict: QUANTIFIED, still OPEN on parity. Regression magnitude measured (231 metrics.md). True sub-minute parity under --no-rcb-time is untestable until a scheduler-side fix exists (out of scope here). Remains OPEN pending 231 pre-regression sub-minute confirmation.

statement: Wedge TRIGGER is a host-pollable listening socket fd (NOT a general gap, NOT the python controller code per se).
reasoning: Single-variable A/B on identical bare busybox with identical --no-rcb-time/-icount/--target-timeslice flags, varying ONLY the injected listening sockets: boot_qemu_off.sh (-serial stdio, no sockets) BOOTS; boot_qemu_filecon.sh (-serial file:, no sockets) BOOTS; boot_qemu_sock.sh (-serial file: + serial-unix + QMP listening sockets) WEDGES at hpet0. The socket chardev is a host-timing-driven pollable fd that, with no PMU preemption, monopolizes turns and starves the -icount vCPU of forward progress at HPET calibration. Matches 05-qemu-boot.py:94-97 inline comment and memory qemu-serial-socket-starves-vcpu-under-hermit.
predicted_evidence: with sockets -> wedge (frozen hpet0); without sockets, same config -> boot to PASS. An extra socket-poller thread present only in the wedge run.
verdict: CONFIRMED (single-variable A/B), REVERSING an earlier wrong 'KILLED/general gap'. 237's same-config diff (wedge-sock vs wedge-filecon) shows the WEDGE has an extra socket-poller thread (clock_gettime x166156 + poll x13846 + read x13846, 32.3% of turns) ABSENT in green; notably the vCPU worker gets ~EQUAL absolute turns in both (289810 vs 292381) -> not aggregate turn-starvation but poller-interleaving preventing HPET calibration completion.

statement: (competing) The wedge is the #1095 guest-clock-lag past-deadline poller (guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC lags committed ~8.5s so an abs-deadline poll is already expired).
reasoning: Pre-#1190, guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC could lag committed_time by ~8.53s (aa5258b: guest ~630.4s vs committed ~639.03s), turning a controller's clock_nanosleep(TIMER_ABSTIME, now+~100ms) into an already-expired sleep that COMMITs (runs immediately) instead of blocking -> busy-poll -> QEMU starved. Competes with H1/H6 as the wedge cause.
predicted_evidence: if the ~8.5s guest-vs-committed lag is ABSENT post-#1190, H7 is KILLED for the current wedge (mechanism is H1/H6, not clock-domain).
verdict: KILLED for the socket-triggered wedge. 237: in the post-#1190 wedge log (hermit @1ece0654), guest CLOCK_MONOTONIC tracks committed_time to ~ms (late reads 1767228032.485..0.553s vs final committed 1767228032.553s), NOT the pre-#1190 ~8.53s lag. #1190 (cc3730fd/3ac51e11 process-tree GuestClock unification) holds; the wedge is not a clock-lag problem.

statement: Spin-boundedness: the --no-rcb-time wedge spin is UNBOUNDED because the burn-out mechanism is MISSING, not merely mistuned. The timeslice/vtime-burn knob (--target-timeslice) is INERT under --no-rcb-time: it does not change the per-turn vtime quantum nor produce escape. The only vtime advancement is via zero-duration SleepUntil(0) polls that advance committed_time WITHOUT delivering the future timed_waiter real work is blocked on. rcb-time (PMU preemption, 'inbound timer preemption event') is the ONLY burn-out, which is why it greens.
reasoning: Sharpens H1(deadline-less vtime starvation)+H2(rcb-time brute-forces committed_time). Owner quant: normal boot=~1.5s vtime; wedge burns ~400x vtime never completing => a timed event due by ~1.5s is starved. Mechanism candidate: scheduler-vtime-jump-unproductive-pollers (step2d jumps committed_time only when run_queue empty; SleepUntil(0) yields keep it non-empty so the jump never fires; no future timed_waiter is serviced).
predicted_evidence: norcb: sweeping K over >=4 orders of magnitude gives NO escape (guest_ts frozen <0.1) and vtime_per_turn (=vtime_burned/turns) INSENSITIVE to K; preempt_events=0 for all K. rcbtime: preempt_events>0 and escape achievable. A pending future timed_waiter (su_future>0) sits at a vtime far below committed while committed races 100s+ ahead, never delivered => LINEAR-vs-K FALSE, burn-out MISSING.
verdict: CONFIRMED. norcb sweep over 4 orders of magnitude of --target-timeslice: vtime_burned FLAT ~490s, guest_ts FLAT ~0.71 (never escapes), preempt_events=0 at EVERY K => INSENSITIVE/non-linear response. Owner's decisive test => burn-out mechanism is MISSING, spin is UNBOUNDED, NOT a tuning problem. Mechanism (E14): guest stuck in ~74ms relative-timeout poll loop (early-boot HPET/timer calibration); Detcore commits each poll-timeout in sequence inflating committed_time ~74ms/poll (~5300 polls -> ~490s vtime) while the vCPU never executes the instructions that finish calibration; ~400x vtime/guest decoupling. rcbtime control (E-rcbtime): preempt_events=380-435 (>0) and knob responds => the sole spin-bounding mechanism is PMU preemption ('inbound timer preemption event'), absent under --no-rcb-time. Evidence E12,E14,E15 + rcbtime control.

statement: UNIFICATION (owner): the ~20% skid-panic and the poller-livelock are ONE bug. After an over-skid the PMU fails to REARM, so 'inbound timer preemption event' stops firing; with no preemption the rcbtime run degrades into the same deadline-less SleepUntil(0) poller-spin as --no-rcb-time (H1/H8). skid -> no rearm -> no preemption -> unbounded spin.
reasoning: Ties H8 (burn-out missing) to the skid evidence in [[demo5-rcb-config-panic-vs-slow-tradeoff]] (RCB-time 4/5 green + 1/5 skid ~20%) and [[pmu-skid-panic-supervisor-hang]] (timer.rs:809 'Clock perf counter exceeds target'). If a skid can occur WITHOUT a fatal panic (overshoot within skid_margin) but still disarm/mis-rearm the PMU alarm, the rcbtime burn-out (H2) silently dies mid-boot and the run wedges. Owner: coordinate with 210 (turn-order).
predicted_evidence: In a rcbtime run that WEDGES (not boots): a skid/'exceeds target'/'perf counter' warning appears, AND the cadence of 'inbound timer preemption event' CEASES at/after that turn while COMMIT turns keep climbing and SleepUntil(0) explodes afterward. CONFIRM if last-preempt-turn << last-COMMIT-turn with a skid marker near the last preempt. KILL if wedged rcbtime runs show preemptions continuing to the end (no rearm failure) or no skid precedes cessation.
verdict: OPEN, needs a genuinely WEDGED rcbtime witness. Naive 'preemption ceased before log-end' signature REFUTED as a wedge indicator (E19): booting runs also show it at the CPU-bound->sleep-driven phase transition (dtid17 last preempt with 0-syscall timeslice, then dtid7 clock_nanosleep). This config (target-timeslice 1e5, max-timeslice 2e8) never wedges (16/20 BOOT_OK, 0 skid, 0 wedge) so route (b) is not reproducible here; the panic-prone rcb-time-time margin config [[demo5-rcb-config-panic-vs-slow-tradeoff]] is where the ~20% skid lives. Synthesis stands: H8 route (a) (--no-rcb-time, preemption never armed, 0 skid) fully accounts for the studied wedge; whether a skid can also disarm an armed PMU mid-boot (route b) is unproven. Hand to 210 (turn-order) + panic-prone config.

statement: The demo5 GREEN regime uses ZERO PMU preemption BY CONSTRUCTION (--max-timeslice disabled), so PMU-skid is NOT on the green path; the fix is to RESTORE the syscall-boundary regime, not to harden PMU-skid.
reasoning: Owner P0 (2026-08-01). Demo config = --strict --no-rcb-time --target-timeslice 100000 --max-timeslice disabled. Source (E17/226): PMU/RCB timer armed only when max_timeslice.is_some(); disabled => None => no PMU timer => 'inbound timer preemption event' can never fire; --target-timeslice is a pure syscall-boundary deadline. Empirics (E17): the demo config yields 0 PMU / 100% syscall-boundary in EVERY run (wedgekit busybox + all full-linux archives); the only PMU-driven boot is the rcb-ON workaround (bbx-green 858 PMU=98.8%). Therefore the historical 1-min green (2a7ca98), running this same 0-PMU-by-construction config, necessarily used ~0 PMU. CONSEQUENCE: PMU-skid robustness is defense-in-depth for the rcb-ON workaround only, NOT the primary green-path fix. The green path is the syscall-boundary regime, which TODAY livelocks on SleepUntil(0) (foundation bug scheduler-vtime-jump-unproductive-pollers); restoring it to green is the fix. Adversarially-evaluable: if ANY archived demo-config (max disabled) run showed >0 'inbound timer preemption event', H10 falls — E17 shows 0 across all of them. CAVEAT: cannot re-demonstrate a green 0-PMU boot at current HEAD (the config wedges); the 2a7ca98 green is not archived, so its 0-PMU regime is inferred from the by-construction argument, not directly counted.
verdict: CONFIRMED at source+config level (0 PMU by construction under --max-timeslice disabled; E17 shows 0 PMU across every demo-config run vs 858 PMU on the rcb-ON workaround). Directly answers owner P0: green did not depend on PMU. Residual: the historical 2a7ca98 green boot is not archived, so its 0-PMU regime is inferred by construction; and the 0-PMU config cannot boot at current HEAD (foundation bug), so 'restore the regime' requires the scheduler-vtime-jump fix.
